scope: 30 candidate products: official-source desk review of platform/pricing/trade-off summaries plus evidence-sensitive original Notion claims. No hands-on tests, medical efficacy assessment, legal opinion, or human publishing approval.

patches.value: Free tier; paid Premium and Premium Pro with monthly, annual, or one-time lifetime options. Story Credits are purchased separately.
patches.reason: Original summary omitted the lifetime option and Premium Pro.

patches.value: English only. Free checking is limited to 500 words at a time and two runs per line-editing report per day; advanced manuscript analyses use separate Story Credits.
patches.reason: Record material language and free-use limitations.

patches.value: iOS, Android, and Web browser access
patches.reason: Official product statement explicitly includes browser access.

patches.value: Windows and macOS (Antidote 12); browser-based Antidote Web; iPhone/iPad (Antidote Mobile dictionaries and guides). Mobile correction uses Antidote Web.
patches.reason: Original summary omitted Mac and conflated product-line platforms with corrector availability.

patches.value: Antidote Mobile provides dictionaries and guides, without the corrector; correction on iPhone/iPad uses Antidote Web. Antidote 12 generative reformulation requires an eligible subscription.
patches.reason: Mobile app support does not imply native mobile grammar correction.

patches.value: Free AGPL-licensed core for self-hosting; optional paid managed Cloud hosting and paid self-hosted Pro features. Infrastructure costs are separate.
patches.reason: Original summary omitted separately paid Pro features.

patches.value: Self-hosting requires server operation; Cloud hosting is paid, and Pro features such as administration and audit logging require a separate paid offer.
patches.reason: Do not generalize free core to all self-hosted features.
Use the source that explicitly states AGPL core licensing; paid Pro is separate.

patches.value: Web; Windows, macOS, and Linux desktop applications; self-hosted deployments
patches.reason: Replace unreviewed desktop OS coverage with official download listing.

patches.value: Paid tiers cover team administration and enterprise features; processing automation uses credits. The repository has MIT-covered code and excluded separately licensed components; check the component license before modification or redistribution.
patches.reason: Mixed licensing makes a blanket MIT or wholly-open-source description inaccurate.

patches.value: Free Cloud tier; paid Cloud plans and a one-time Believer offer. The EE backend has separate authorization requirements for modification, compilation, or redistribution.
patches.reason: Pricing page states compilation restrictions and offers a one-time plan.

patches.value: The core editor is MIT-licensed; the EE backend is separately licensed, with authorization required for modification, compilation, or redistribution. Desktop and mobile feature coverage differs.
patches.reason: Keep core-editor open-source=true under the existing attribute definition, while exposing backend and platform scope.

patches.value: Joplin uses Markdown note content and supports Markdown import/export, but its local profile stores notes and metadata in SQLite. It is not a vault of directly edited Markdown files. Paid Cloud storage and collaboration limits depend on plan.
patches.reason: Current markdown-files definition includes a supported note format, so true remains valid; explain storage rather than mislabeling the boolean false.
License page was attached to a Markdown-storage claim without proving that claim.
